records.place: Dernau, in the middle Ahr valley, Ahr

wine.name: Dernauer Pfarrwingert Spätburgunder GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs: the dry wine of a site the VDP ranks Grosse Lage
wine.sites: The Pfarrwingert, the parish vineyard above Dernau, a VDP.Grosse Lage on grainy greywacke and weathered slate with some clay slate; the soils warm quickly, and the VDP counts it among the hottest sites of the Ahr.
wine.making: The grapes are picked by hand into small crates and ferment with their own wild yeasts, macerating on the skins for about three weeks. The wine then rests on its fine lees in barriques, about a third of them new, for some eighteen months, and a further six months in bottle; it is bottled unfiltered, by the estate's own account of the wine.
wine.glass: Sour cherry over wild herbs, rose and cracked pepper, with the smoke and iron that slate gives; fine boned rather than broad, with fresh acidity, fine tannin and a long, cool finish.
wine.ageing: Tight for its first few years, it opens after five to eight, and a strong vintage holds its fruit for well over a decade.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a wide Burgundy glass.

label.means: The parish vineyard of Dernau; labels have printed it as Dernauer Pfarrwingert and as Dernau Pfarrwingert.
The German name for Pinot Noir, the grape of most of the Ahr's slopes.
Great growth, often shortened to GG: the VDP's dry wine from a site it ranks Grosse Lage.

records.table: Meyer-Näkel's Dernauer Pfarrwingert Spätburgunder GG is dry Pinot Noir from the parish vineyard above Dernau, on warm greywacke and slate in the Ahr valley. Sour cherry, wild herbs and smoke sit on a fine, fresh frame; pour it as you would a red Burgundy.
records.story: The Näkel family had grown vines at Dernau for generations when the estate took its present shape there in 1950, at a time when the Ahr sold most of its red as pale, often sweetish wine to day trippers from the Rhineland. In the 1980s the founder's son, who gave up teaching for the vineyard, took the house further: Spätburgunder fermented long on its skins and aged in small oak barrels, from steep holdings on slate and greywacke at Dernau, Walporzheim and Neuenahr. Wine writers credit him with starting the valley's modern dry red. The estate joined the VDP, Germany's association of Prädikat estates, in 1994, and when the association ranked its members' vineyards, the Pfarrwingert became a Grosse Lage, whose dry wine is labelled Grosses Gewächs. His two daughters later took the estate on. On 14 July 2021 the flood that tore down the Ahr damaged nearly every wine estate in the valley, Dernau among the villages hit, and the family rebuilt. For a sommelier the Pfarrwingert is the Ahr in one glass: Pinot Noir from slate at the northern edge of red wine country, cool, perfumed and firm.

others.name: Walporzheimer Kräuterberg Spätburgunder GG
others.note: From the steep, terraced Kräuterberg at Walporzheim, a Grosse Lage; the warmer, firmer of the house's two Grosses Gewächs of note.

others.name: Spätburgunder Blauschiefer
others.note: A Spätburgunder named for the valley's blue slate, the house's step into its style.

traps: Pfarrwingert lies at Dernau and the Kräuterberg at Walporzheim; both are Grosse Lagen of Meyer-Näkel, so the village on the label tells them apart.
A Grosses Gewächs is always dry and carries no Prädikat such as Spätlese or Auslese on its label.
Ahr Spätburgunder grows on slate and greywacke, unlike the limestone and loess of Baden's reds, and it shows in a cooler, firmer wine.

report: founded is left empty: the estate in its present form dates from 1950 in two secondary accounts (wein.plus and the vieduvin profile), but the family calls itself the fifth generation of winegrowers and a wine database gives the family two hundred years at the site, so the story says the estate took its present shape in 1950.

The year the founder's son took over, 1982, is in one wine guide only, and 1987 as the first dry barrique vintage in one wiki only, so the story says the 1980s; his teaching career is from the VDP's own page on its pin of honour.

The label's form changes by year: Falstaff lists Dernauer Pfarrwingert (2015) and Dernau Pfarrwingert (2013, 2022, 2023), and the estate's own page prints PFARRWINGERT Spätburgunder VDP.GROSSES GEWÄCHS, so the label term says both and the name keeps the plan's words.

The making (wild yeasts, about twenty days on the skins, eighteen months in barrique with thirty per cent new, six months in bottle, unfiltered) is the estate's sheet for its 2022 vintage, hedged as recent vintages; the glass draws on the library's note (sour cherry, iron, smoke) and the Vinum guide's quoted on the estate's site (herbs, roses, pepper).

The flood damage to the estate itself is in one secondary account (Discover Germany); the story says only that the flood hit Dernau and nearly every estate, as the VDP's flood appeal reports, and that the family rebuilt.
No living person is named: the founder's son and his two daughters are living; the founder's dates were not found, so he is not named.

records.place: Rech, in the middle Ahr valley, Ahr

wine.name: Recher Herrenberg Spätburgunder GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Herrenberg, the one VDP.Grosse Lage of Rech
wine.grapes: Spätburgunder, Pinot Noir, alone, much of it from old vines on their own roots.
wine.sites: The Herrenberg above Rech, a steep, terraced, south facing slope between about 130 and 230 metres beneath the Schwedenkopf rock, on stony soil of slate and greywacke; many of its vines are ungrafted, the VDP notes.
wine.making: The grapes are picked by hand and strictly sorted, then ferment on their skins for about three weeks. The malolactic fermentation takes place in barrique, and the wine ages for about nineteen months in new barriques before bottling, as the house describes it.
wine.glass: Morello and sour cherry over tobacco, black tea and freshly ground pepper, with a seam of slate; firm, concentrated and long, the new oak plain when young and folding in with time.
wine.ageing: Marked by its new oak in youth, it wants six to eight years, and a strong vintage keeps for well over a decade.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour or two; a wide Burgundy glass.

label.means: The Herrenberg of Rech; labels have printed both Recher Herrenberg and Rech Herrenberg.
The red wine estate: the house's own description, printed beside its name.
Short for Grosses Gewächs, the VDP's dry wine from a site it ranks Grosse Lage.

records.table: Jean Stodden's Recher Herrenberg Spätburgunder GG comes from old, often ungrafted vines on the steep slate and greywacke slope above Rech in the Ahr. Raised in new barriques, it is firm and dense, with sour cherry and pepper, so decant it and give it years.
records.story: The Stodden family traces its winegrowing at Rech, in the middle of the Ahr valley, to 1578, by its own account, and in 1900 a forebear began to press the family's own Spätburgunder, the step from which the house dates its own wine. For most of the twentieth century the Ahr was known for light, often sweetish red sold to visitors from the Rhineland; the family's later generations turned the estate towards dry Pinot Noir fermented on its skins and raised in barrique, and it came to call itself Das Rotweingut, the red wine estate, with Spätburgunder on the great majority of its vines and a little Frühburgunder and Riesling beside it. Its heart is the Herrenberg, the steep slope beneath the Schwedenkopf rock whose name, the house says, recalls the lords of Saffenburg, to whose lands Rech belonged. The estate joined the VDP in 2005, and the Herrenberg, the one Grosse Lage of Rech, gives its Grosses Gewächs. On 14 July 2021 the flood that swept the Ahr damaged nearly every wine estate in the valley, as the VDP reports, Rech among the villages on the river. For a sommelier the Herrenberg GG shows the Ahr at its most concentrated: old vines, long skin contact and all new oak.

others.name: Recher Herrenberg Frühburgunder GG
others.note: The early ripening Pinot mutation from the same slope, a Grosses Gewächs of its own.

others.name: Dernau Hardtberg Spätburgunder GG
others.note: From the Hardtberg at Dernau, a further Grosse Lage whose Spätburgunder the house bottles as a Grosses Gewächs.

traps: The Herrenberg of Rech is an Ahr Grosse Lage; the Herrenberg of Ungstein in the Pfalz and the Herrenberger of Wawern on the Saar are different sites.
The Recher Herrenberg GG is aged in new barriques throughout, so a young bottle shows its oak more plainly than most Ahr reds.
Jean Stodden is a family estate at Rech, not a merchant's brand; the name on the label is the house's, not that of a single living winemaker.

cards.front: Jean Stodden's Herrenberg: which village does it overlook, and what rank does the VDP give it?
cards.back: Rech, in the middle Ahr valley; it is the one VDP.Grosse Lage of the village.

cards.front: By the house's account, how long and in what is Jean Stodden's Recher Herrenberg GG aged?
cards.back: About nineteen months in new barriques, after the malolactic fermentation in barrel.

questions.q: A guest asks how Jean Stodden raises its Recher Herrenberg Spätburgunder GG in the cellar. Which description fits?
opts: About nineteen months in new barriques
Two years in large old oak casks
questions.exp: The house ages the Herrenberg GG about nineteen months in new barriques; a short stay in used barrels or large old casks would mark it far less.

questions.q: From which year does the Stodden family of Rech trace its winegrowing, by its own account?
questions.exp: The house dates its winegrowing to 1578; 1900 is when a forebear began to press the family's own wine, and 2005 when the estate joined the VDP.

report: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. founded is left empty as the plan asks: the house dates its winegrowing to 1578 and its own wine to 1900, when a forebear began to press it, and neither is the founding of the estate as such.
The forebear of 1900 is named on the house's page (Alois Stodden) but his dates were not found, so he is described, not named; the house's head is living and is not named.

The VDP's Herrenberg page disagrees with itself on the site (130 to 230 metres in its text, 170 to 190 in its table; greywacke and loam in the table, slate and greywacke of volcanic origin in the text), so the record gives the text's range and slate and greywacke.

The making (about three weeks on the skins, malolactic in barrique, about nineteen months in new barriques) is the house's own page; the glass draws on Falstaff's notes for the 2012 and 2013 vintages and the house's own note (spice, fruit, precision).
The Wine Society gives the vines on the Herrenberg as 80 years old and ungrafted, a figure in one source, so the record says old and often ungrafted, which the VDP's page supports.
Whether Jean is said in the French way is not confirmed by a source; the respelling follows the French form and a checker may prefer only the surname.

records.place: Ahrweiler, with the Gärkammer at Walporzheim, Ahr

wine.name: Walporzheimer Gärkammer Spätburgunder GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Gärkammer, a VDP.Grosse Lage held whole by the family
wine.grapes: Spätburgunder, Pinot Noir, alone, part of it from ungrafted vines up to a century old.
wine.sites: The Gärkammer at Walporzheim, a steep, terraced, south facing site, tiny and held by the family alone; its dark stone walls and weathered slate store the day's heat into the night.
wine.making: The grapes are picked by hand and fermented on their skins, and the wine is then matured in barriques of French oak; the house has favoured used barrels over new for its reds, as the VDP described its cellar in 2020.
wine.glass: Wild cherry, elderberry and wild strawberry over slate, black pepper and a dark, tarry depth, with mallow and mint in some years; dense yet fresh, with fine tannin and a long, savoury finish.
wine.ageing: Closed for its first few years, it opens after five or so, and a good vintage keeps for fifteen years and more.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a wide Burgundy glass.

label.means: Fermenting chamber: a name the VDP ties to the heat the site holds in summer.
Printed instead of Spätburgunder on some later labels of the wine; the same grape.
Short for Grosses Gewächs, the VDP's dry wine from a site it ranks Grosse Lage.

records.table: J.J. Adeneuer's Walporzheimer Gärkammer Spätburgunder GG comes from a tiny walled terrace at Walporzheim that the family holds alone, where dark slate keeps the heat into the night. Expect wild cherry, pepper and slate on a dense, fresh frame.
records.story: The Adeneuer family has made wine at Ahrweiler for centuries, and by its own account it has held the Gärkammer, a small walled terrace of slate above Walporzheim, alone since the early eighteenth century: the house's pages give 1714 and 1716. The name means fermenting chamber, and the VDP ties it to the heat that the dark rock and the walls store through the summer. For most of the twentieth century the Ahr was known for light, often sweetish red sold to visitors from the Rhineland; the estate's reds are dry Spätburgunder raised in French barriques. When the VDP ranked its members' vineyards, the Gärkammer became a Grosse Lage, and the family calls it the smallest in Germany, the VDP the smallest of the Ahr, planted to Spätburgunder alone and partly to ungrafted vines up to a century old. Because one family holds it whole, its Grosses Gewächs is a monopole wine, and a second wine of the site, Kleine Kammer, the small chamber, shares its name. A younger generation of the family joined the estate in 2015, and on 14 July 2021 the flood that swept the Ahr damaged nearly every wine estate in the valley, as the VDP reports. For a sommelier the Gärkammer is the lesson of a monopole in one bottle: one family, one small site and one wine.

others.name: Kleine Kammer
others.note: The small chamber: a second Pinot Noir from the Gärkammer, bottled as a dry wine rather than a Grosses Gewächs.

others.name: Ahrweiler Rosenthal Spätburgunder GG
others.note: A Grosses Gewächs from the Rosenthal at Ahrweiler, a further Grosse Lage of the house.

traps: The Gärkammer is held by the Adeneuer family alone; the Kräuterberg, another Grosse Lage at Walporzheim, is shared by several houses, Meyer-Näkel among them.
Later labels may print Walporzheim and Pinot Noir where older ones read Walporzheimer and Spätburgunder; it is the same site and the same grape.

report: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. founded is left empty: one wine guide gives 1776, another wine since 1635 at Ahrweiler, the VDP's estate page sole family ownership since 1714 and the house's product page the Gärkammer since 1716, so the record says the early eighteenth century for the site and gives no founding.

The size claim is hedged as the family's: the house calls the Gärkammer the smallest single site in Germany at 0.68 hectares and the VDP's estate page quotes the family calling it the smallest VDP.Grosse Lage in Germany, while the VDP's site page says one of Germany's smallest and the smallest of the Ahr; the plan's why says the VDP calls it the smallest in Germany, which is the family's quote on the VDP's page.

The making is thin: no source gave the maceration or the months in barrel for the Gärkammer; the VDP's page of 2020 says every wine but the Blanc de Noir is aged in used French barriques, so the record says used barrels were favoured, hedged to 2020.
The label's form changes: Falstaff lists Walporzheimer Gärkammer (2006, 2007, 2011) and Walporzheim Gärkammer, with Pinot Noir for the 2022; the house's page heads its 2023 simply GÄRKAMMER.
The glass draws on Falstaff's notes for the 2007, 2020 and 2022 vintages; the younger generation's arrival in 2015 is the house's own team page, and he is living and not named.
The Kastenholz clone of the old vines (house page) is left out as one source's claim.

wine.name: Mayschosser Mönchberg Spätburgunder GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Mönchberg, a VDP.Grosse Lage of Mayschoss
wine.sites: The Mönchberg, the terraced, south facing slope that rings the estate at Mayschoss like an amphitheatre, at about 200 to 220 metres on greywacke with a little loam, held up by walls of slate.
wine.making: The grapes go by the bucket into the fermenting vat, and the house has fermented with wild yeasts since the 1980s. The wine then spends about twelve months in new barriques of French oak and some six months more in used barrels, by the estate's own account.
wine.glass: Blackcurrant, blackberry and dark chocolate with fine spice and a cool, slaty edge; firm yet elegant, with fresh acidity, fine tannin and a long finish.
wine.ageing: Tight in its first years, it opens after five or six and keeps well beyond a decade in a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for an hour; a wide Burgundy glass, with lamb or game.

label.means: The monks' hill above Mayschoss, named for the monastery said to have owned it.
The upper valley village of the Ahr where the estate and the Mönchberg lie.
Short for Grosses Gewächs, the VDP's dry wine from a site it ranks Grosse Lage.

records.table: Deutzerhof's Mayschosser Mönchberg Spätburgunder GG grows on the terraced greywacke slope that wraps round the estate at Mayschoss in the upper Ahr. A year in new French oak frames blackcurrant and dark chocolate; serve it with lamb or game.
records.story: A grower named Caspar Cossmann appears in a debt register of Are castle in 1574, and the Cossmann family of Mayschoss counts its winegrowing from him, by the estate's own account. Mayschoss is also the home of the Winzerverein founded there in December 1868, which the German Wine Institute calls the first wine growers' cooperative. In 1952 the family left the cooperative to make and sell wine under its own name, and the estate later took the name Deutzerhof. The VDP notes accounts that the Mönchberg belonged to an outpost of the Benedictine abbey of Deutz in Cologne, though others name the abbey of Klosterrath near Aachen. In 1980 the son in law of the house moved the estate to its present site at the foot of the Mönchberg and turned the cellar to fermentation with wild yeasts; dry Spätburgunder raised in barrique became its calling. When the VDP ranked its members' vineyards, the Mönchberg became a Grosse Lage. In 2020 the family handed Deutzerhof to a long standing friend of the house, and the following year the flood of 14 July 2021 swept the valley. For a sommelier the Mönchberg GG is the upper Ahr's steep greywacke in a glass, framed by new oak.

The VDP lists more than one vineyard named Mönchberg, so the village, Mayschoss, matters on the label.
Deutzerhof has nothing to do with the Champagne house Deutz; it is a family founded estate of the Ahr.

wine.name: Dernauer Hardtberg Frühburgunder GG
wine.classification: VDP.Grosses Gewächs from the Hardtberg, a VDP.Grosse Lage of Dernau
wine.grapes: Frühburgunder alone: the early ripening mutation of Pinot Noir, known in France as Pinot Noir Précoce.
wine.sites: The Hardtberg at Dernau, where the estate's vines lie in the upper Eigelstal, a side valley, on the Devonian slate that runs through all its holdings.
wine.making: Frühburgunder ripens two to three weeks before Spätburgunder and is picked first. Like every dry red of the house, the wine is aged in barriques, part of them new French oak; Falstaff recorded seventeen months in barrique for the 2019 vintage.
wine.glass: Wild cherry and dark forest berries over smoky, peppery slate; creamy at first without weight, with ripe acidity and fine grained tannin, softer and darker than a Spätburgunder of the valley.
wine.ageing: Open sooner than a Spätburgunder of like rank, it gains for five to eight years and keeps for longer in a strong vintage.
wine.serve: 15 to 17 degrees Celsius; decant a young bottle for half an hour; a wide Burgundy glass.

label.means: Early Burgundian: the early ripening mutation of Pinot Noir, a speciality of the Ahr.
The Grosse Lage at Dernau where the wine grows, in the upper Eigelstal.
Up in the Eigelstal: the name the estate gives its 2023 Frühburgunder GG from Dernau.
Short for Grosses Gewächs, the VDP's dry wine from a site it ranks Grosse Lage.

records.table: Kreuzberg's Dernauer Hardtberg GG is Frühburgunder, the Ahr's early ripening Pinot, from the Hardtberg at Dernau on Devonian slate. Wild cherry and forest berries over smoky slate, softer and darker than Spätburgunder; decant it briefly.
records.story: Kreuzberg dates itself to 1953, when the managing clerk of the Dernau growers' cooperative founded an estate of his own in the village. His son ran it for more than forty years with his wife, his sister and her husband, and enlarged it, and in 1994 he handed it to his own son, then 29, who set the house on Spätburgunder of high ambition. The estate joined the VDP, Germany's association of Prädikat estates, in 2000, and its vineyards on Devonian slate at Dernau, Ahrweiler and Neuenahr were ranked by the association; by its own account every one may give a Grosses Gewächs. Beside Spätburgunder it grows Frühburgunder, the early ripening mutation of Pinot Noir that the Ahr keeps as its speciality, and its Grosses Gewächs of Frühburgunder from the Hardtberg at Dernau is the wine of the house that wine guides and prizes single out. On 14 July 2021 the flood that swept the Ahr struck the estate hard, the VDP reports, and the team moved to temporary quarters at Meckenheim, about 20 kilometres away. In February 2024 the sale of its wine returned to Dernau. For a sommelier the Hardtberg GG is the chance to pour the Ahr's own grape: Pinot Noir's early cousin, darker and softer, from Dernau slate.

sources.title: Weingut Kreuzberg: 2023 Oben im Eigelstal, Dernau Frühburgunder GG
Falstaff: Weingut H. J. Kreuzberg, Dernau Hardtberg Frühburgunder GG 2019

report: SWAP OF THE WINE PROPOSED: the plan's flagship, a Dernauer Hardtberg Spätburgunder GG, was not found for Kreuzberg in any source but one wiki; the estate's own site, Falstaff (2009 to 2019) and Meininger list its Hardtberg GG as Frühburgunder, and its Spätburgunder GGs come from the Sonnenberg, Silberberg and Schieferlay. The record is written for the Hardtberg Frühburgunder GG, so wine.name breaks the plan's words until plan.json's wine is changed to Dernauer Hardtberg Frühburgunder GG (the key kreuzberg kept).

If the read together agent prefers a Spätburgunder flagship, the Neuenahr Sonnenberg Spätburgunder GG is the house's listed alternative; the Hardtberg Spätburgunder GG Falstaff lists belongs to Jean Stodden, not Kreuzberg.

founded 1953 is the estate's own front page (Seit 1953) with the Decanter date the plan's note gives; the history page itself gives no year. The founder, his son and grandson are not named: the founder's dates were not found, and the son and grandson are living.

The estate's 2023 Frühburgunder GG is sold as Oben im Eigelstal on a page whose address began as the 2022 Hardtberg; that it is the same wine renamed rests on that page and Falstaff's 2023 listing, and is hedged.

The making is thin: only that every dry red is aged in barriques with new French oak for the top wines (the house) and seventeen months for 2019 (Falstaff); the glass is Falstaff's 2019 note with the region record's softer, darker for Frühburgunder.
The Mayschoss cooperative of 1868 is told in Deutzerhof's story, as the plan's note allowed, and not here.
